description: Sort contract fixtures (Paket 9, Phase B), JS only (Sort has no Rust implementation), run by tests/unit/sort-contract.test.ts. 'expected' is the BINDING TARGET behaviour of the contract below, written by hand from the rules (never generated from an engine). 'current' documents the output of the current implementation (src/utils/sortLines.ts) where it differs from the target; a case without 'current' already behaves as targeted. Until Phase C the tests assert 'current' (or 'expected' if there is none) against the real sortText, so the suite stays green and every deviation is visible here; Phase C removes 'current' and the target becomes the assertion. 'basis': 'decision' = follows directly from a product decision of Phase B, 'derived' = follows from the rules but was not decided explicitly (confirmation requested, see docs/analyse/Paket9-PhaseB-Sortiervertrag.md). 'rules' and 'finding' (F1-F9, Phase A report) are references. 'icuNumeric': the target equals a stable sort with Intl.Collator('de', { numeric: true }) (plus the blank-line rule), checked as fixture consistency. 'openDecisions' are NOT binding: every candidate states its full result ('losesLine': the candidate knowingly loses a line in the text representation), 'recommended' is a proposal or null. 'properties' are corpora of equivalence classes in target order: any input order must give the classes in this order, each class in input order. 'random' has no golden order.

rules.R1: Empty and whitespace-only lines are data lines: they are kept and placed after all other lines, in input order, for ascending and descending order and every deterministic method. Whitespace = the Unicode White_Space set of Paket 8 (src/utils/diff/whitespace.ts, isBlankLine): U+0085 is whitespace, U+FEFF and U+200B are not.
rules.R2: Alphabetical order is ICU collation with the explicit locale 'de' (never the host locale); whitespace and punctuation are not ignored, digits are characters (no numeric collation).
rules.R3: caseSensitive false: case is ignored, accents stay relevant (sensitivity 'accent'). caseSensitive true: case is an additional tertiary criterion of the collation (sensitivity 'variant'; for 'de' lowercase sorts before uppercase).
rules.R4: Lines with equal sort keys keep their input order (stable sort).
rules.R5: Reverse methods reverse the comparison, not the finished array: equal keys keep their input order, blank lines stay at the end.
rules.R6: Line length counts Unicode code points, not UTF-16 code units (a lone surrogate counts as one).
rules.R7: No implicit trim: leading and trailing whitespace is part of the sort key and of the output.
rules.R8: An unknown sort method (also an empty, differently cased or non-string value) is a controlled input error { error: 'invalidMode' }, never a silent default.
rules.R9: Line model of Paket 6 unchanged: LF, CRLF, CR; the result uses the most frequent line ending of the input (tie: the first one) and keeps the trailing newline.
rules.N1: Natural (derived): the same collation as alphabetical (R2, R3) with runs of ASCII digits compared by their numeric value, like Intl.Collator('de', { numeric: true }): a number sorts where a digit sorts (after whitespace and punctuation, before letters), any length without precision loss.
rules.N2: Natural (decision): negative numbers. Derived boundary: '-' is a sign when it directly precedes a digit and stands at the line start or after whitespace; elsewhere see openDecisions OD-1 to OD-3.
rules.N3: Natural (decision): the decimal separator is the point. A line that consists only of a (signed) decimal number is compared by its value ('1.10' = 1.1). The comma is never a decimal separator. Decimal points inside text: OD-4, OD-5.
rules.N4: Natural (decision): a number directly after a letter is a part of a label: 'v1.2' sorts before 'v1.10' (the point separates parts).
rules.N5: Natural (decision): no special interpretation of dates, hexadecimal numbers or scientific notation; such text is compared by N1 to N4 only.

openDecisions.question: Is '-' directly after a letter or digit a sign (Datei-2, ISO dates)?

A.rule: no sign after a letter or digit, '-' is text

B.rule: '-' before a digit is always a sign

openDecisions.question: Same rule for ISO dates (consequence of OD-1)

A.rule: no sign after a digit: the parts are compared as numbers

B.rule: '-' before a digit is always a sign: -12 < -02

openDecisions.question: Is '-' after punctuation (brackets, colon, slash) a sign?

A.rule: sign only at the line start or after whitespace; '-' after '(' is punctuation and sorts before digits

openDecisions.question: Which characters are signs: only ASCII '-', or also '+' and U+2212 (minus sign)?

A.rule: only ASCII '-'; U+2212 is a symbol and sorts before digits

openDecisions.question: When is 'x.y' inside text a decimal number and when a multi-part label (chapters, versions)?

A.rule: a decimal only when the whole line is the number; inside text the point separates parts

B.rule: a decimal when the number stands at the line start or after whitespace (same boundary as the sign)

openDecisions.question: Same rule for prices inside text (consequence of OD-4)

A.rule: inside text the point separates parts: 5 < 25 < 125
a number with more than one point is a multi-part label

B.rule: the first 'x.y' is a decimal (1.10 = 1.1), the rest are parts

openDecisions.question: Numerically equal spellings (1, 1.0, 1.00, 01): equal keys or tie-break by text?

A.rule: equal value = equal key, input order kept

B.rule: equal value, then the text decides by collation: independent of the input order

openDecisions.question: Negative zero and leading zeros (consequence of OD-6)

A.rule: equal value = equal key, input order kept

B.rule: equal value, then the text decides by collation

openDecisions.question: An empty line moved to the end of a text without trailing newline cannot be told apart from a trailing newline (Paket 6 text representation). Keep R9 (the empty line disappears in the text) or add a trailing newline so that no line is lost?

A.rule: R9 unchanged: no trailing newline is added; the result text reads as 2 lines plus trailing newline (one line less)

B.rule: if the last result line is empty and the input has no trailing newline, a trailing newline is added: all 3 lines survive

openDecisions.question: Random: do blank lines take part in the shuffle or stay at the end (R1)?

B.rule: non-blank lines are shuffled, blank lines stay at the end in input order

random.note: Six permutations, chi-square with 5 degrees of freedom; 20.515 is the 0.999 quantile. Math.random is replaced by a seeded generator, so the run is reproducible. Current: sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5) (F3) is far above the critical value. Target (Phase C, Fisher-Yates with an injectable random source): below it.
